purpose: Reserve one primary research direction for candidates that surfaced in a neighboring search shard, so later direction panels cannot publish the same functional object under different names.
rules: A candidate may be searched from multiple directions, but it can have only one primary publication direction.
Routing is not acceptance, ranking, or a blind-review score.
The primary direction is chosen by the claimed research object and decisive experiment, not by the paper or repository where the issue was first observed.
A later panel may reroute a candidate only by recording the old and new direction plus a non-cosmetic change in claim boundary.

reservations.reason: The estimand is the action-level harm of a naturally produced cooperative-perception ghost under accurate V2X input.
The research object is substitution between explicit inter-agent messages and implicit vehicle-motion signals in cooperative driving.
The decisive variable is cross-agent error correlation at fixed marginal perception quality.
The proposed bound concerns whether another traffic participant's intent is identifiable before an irreversible cooperative maneuver.
The core problem is learning a fast/slow reasoning policy when the unchosen reasoning branch has non-randomly missing utility.
The claim tests whether an agent's failure explanation identifies which internal repair intervention causally restores behavior.
The claimed failure is a reasoning monitor becoming miscalibrated when observed CoT quality and action-causal influence separate.
The candidate distinguishes language generalization from persistent policy-memory retrieval on the same simulator state.
The contribution is a benchmark evaluator correction for prediction-dependent question coverage and method ranking.
The research object is selection bias in an evaluation aggregate that computes quality only on successful episodes.
The decisive result is whether the benchmark's prefix success event changes policy ranking relative to full maneuver completion.
The empirical null separates natural closed-loop stochastic deviation from attack-induced excess risk in a security benchmark.
The claimed hazard is an invalid generated token silently aliasing to an executable driving action at a security-sensitive interface.
The experiment asks whether retrieved visual context contributes beyond GPS and route priors to an end-to-end driving output.
The action interface combines path and speed from separate heads into a control not proposed by either complete trajectory.
The shared generation budget can trade language tokens against the physical trajectory horizon of an end-to-end VLA.
The decisive ablation tests whether language-conditioned trajectory gains come from future-motion information embedded in captions.
The claimed effect is test-time candidate scaling amplifying trajectory-verifier error in end-to-end planning.
The contribution is an episode-level evaluation and risk accounting protocol for repeated verifier calls.
